title: Stable chunks arrive while speaking
instruction: Arm the test, double tap Right Option, read the full script, then tap Right Option once.
script: I want the transcript to appear while I am still speaking, one stable phrase at a time, so I can see a mistake before I reach the end of this sentence.
manualChecks: The overlay stayed readable while the destination filled

title: Premature stop keeps useful text
instruction: Stop immediately after the words ‘yellow marker’. Do not read the grey remainder.
script: The first useful section ends at the yellow marker. The grey remainder should never be spoken or inserted.
spokenUntil: The first useful section ends at the yellow marker.
manualChecks: The overlay showed what had been captured before the early stop

title: Punctuation and contractions
instruction: Read naturally; do not dictate punctuation names.
script: I’m not convinced it’s broken, but I can’t ship it today. If the final check passes, we’ll release it tomorrow; otherwise, we won’t.
manualChecks: Sentence punctuation looked natural

title: Paths, addresses and numbers
instruction: Say the symbols as you normally would when dictating technical work.
script: Send the result to hello@example.com, keep the threshold at 70%, and save the report under ~/dev/native/dictation/results before build 402.
manualChecks: The destination remained easy to inspect as technical tokens arrived

title: Ordinary symbol words stay ordinary
instruction: Read naturally. None of these ordinary phrases should become symbols.
script: Calculate the dot product, discuss slash fiction, and meet Ian at five before lunch.

title: Terminal-safe agent request
instruction: Read the request exactly. Terminal visibility is validated separately against the real coding-agent TUI.
script: Run swift test, inspect the first failure, and fix the implementation without weakening the assertion. Do not commit, push, or touch the unrelated settings files.

title: Code-shaped words and flags
instruction: Read the script as written, including the flag and file names.
script: Open Sources slash DictationApp slash AppDelegate dot swift, keep the main actor annotation, run git diff double dash check, and never force unwrap the event.

title: Explicit spoken symbols
instruction: Say dot, slash and dash dash exactly where shown.
script: Open dot context, inspect tilde slash Documents slash Research slash notes dot txt, and run tool dash dash verbose.

title: Focused control changes mid-sentence
instruction: Keep reading normally. The runner will change focus automatically while you speak and read the recovery clipboard after stop.
script: This sentence began in the first control, but I moved focus before saying that the complete transcript must be recovered safely.
manualChecks: No transcript text appeared in the secondary control
The app reported that the transcript was copied

title: Window or tab changes mid-sentence
instruction: Keep reading normally. The runner will move focus automatically to simulate the destination changing.
script: I started this dictation in the original tab, then changed tabs, and the full transcript should be on the clipboard instead of being sprayed into the new destination.
manualChecks: Nothing was typed into the newly focused tab
The app reported recovery

title: Existing personal correction
instruction: Pronounce the domain as ‘en dot is’ so the recogniser is likely to produce en.is.
script: Open en.is and compare the latest note with the Portman repository before changing anything.

title: Teach a correction by voice
instruction: Speak the whole command. The destination should stay empty because this is an app command.
script: Hey Dictation, you just transcribed it as port man but what I actually said was Portman p-o-r-t-m-a-n can you add that to my rules so you remember for next time.
manualChecks: The overlay confirmed that the correction was remembered
The Corrections Markdown contains port man to Portman

title: Spoken correction works next time
instruction: Run this immediately after the correction command scenario.
script: Open the port man project and inspect the current branch before running any tests.

title: Correction respects phrase boundaries
instruction: This checks that a short rule does not rewrite text inside a longer word.
script: Open en.is, but leave the word open.island exactly as it is because that longer token is unrelated.

title: Filler and repeated-phrase cleanup
instruction: Include every filler and repeated phrase; Clean runs locally as soon as you stop.
script: Um, I need to, I need to send the report today, erm, but first check whether the figures from Tuesday are actually final.
forbidden: I need to, I need to
manualChecks: Nothing was inserted before you stopped

title: Cleanup cannot drop protected facts
instruction: Speak naturally with the fillers. The guarded output must retain every exact technical fact.
script: Uh, email ian@example.com when build 402 reaches 70%, and, erm, save the log at ~/dev/native/dictation/output.json.

title: Cleanup keeps tone and profanity
instruction: Do not soften the wording while reading it.
script: Erm, the current dialog is fucking annoying because it steals focus every time, and I want that fixed without redesigning the whole app.
manualChecks: The result still sounded like the speaker

title: Direct email without invented ceremony
instruction: The model should format this as an email body but invent no recipient, greeting or sign-off.
script: Um, can you send the revised figures by Thursday afternoon? I need them before the finance call at half past three, and please flag anything that changed since Monday.
forbidden: I hope this email finds you well
manualChecks: Paragraph breaks helped without making the message corporate

title: Email preserves uncertainty
instruction: The result must not turn a tentative statement into a promise.
script: I think I can have the first draft ready on Friday, but I am not completely sure until the data import finishes tomorrow morning.

title: Structure a rough article thought
instruction: Speak the rough thought as one stream. Judge the result as prose, not verbatim dictation.
script: The useful thing about building your own dictation app is not having another product to maintain, it is being able to notice the tiny delays and awkward behaviours that commercial tools accept, like pasting one huge block into a terminal or hiding the transcript when you stop too early. Once those are measurable you can make the boring path feel instant, and that matters more to me than adding a long list of clever modes.
manualChecks: The structure improved the thought without inventing a conclusion
The voice still felt direct and personal

title: Article mode invents no evidence
instruction: There are deliberately no statistics or external sources in the script.
script: I used the app for a few days and the main thing I noticed was that seeing words arrive changed how confidently I dictated. That is only my experience, not a study, and I do not want to pretend it proves anything for other people.

title: Long transcript stays readable
instruction: Read the full paragraph while watching the overlay scroll and the destination continue to fill.
script: This is a deliberately longer dictation to check that the overlay remains useful after several lines of text. I should be able to glance at the newest words without losing the earlier context completely, and the target field should continue receiving stable chunks without freezing, jumping focus, duplicating a phrase, or waiting until the very end to show everything at once. When I stop, the remaining tail should arrive quickly and the menu should still offer the finished transcript if I need to copy it again.
manualChecks: The newest words remained visible in the overlay
The overlay did not take keyboard focus
Stop felt effectively immediate

title: Rapid consecutive sessions
instruction: Dictate this, stop, wait for the overlay to close, then immediately start and dictate it again into the same field.
script: The second session should start cleanly without repeating any words from the first session or waiting for the speech model to load again.
manualChecks: The second overlay opened immediately
No transcript from the first session leaked into the second
